ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (كَالُوهُمْ): there are two views on «هُمْ». First: it is an attached object pronoun, and the implied form is «كَالُوا لَهُمْ» (they measured for them).
It is also said that this verb is sometimes transitive by itself and sometimes through a preposition, and the object here is omitted, i.e. «كَالُوهُمُ الطَّعَامَ» (they measured out the food for them) and the like. On this view «كَالُوا» and «وَزَنُوا» are not written with the alif.
The second view: it is a detached pronoun emphasising the agent pronoun; on this view the two are written with the alif.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُولَئِكَ أَنَّهُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (أَلَا يَظُنُّ): the origin is the negating (لَا), which the interrogative hamza has entered; it is not the (أَلَا) of drawing attention (tanbīh), because what follows that one is affirmative, whereas here it is negated.

ukberi-tibyan:5-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ (٥) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٦) كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ): it is a badal (substitute) for the position of the preposition and its genitive noun.
It is also said that the implied form is «يُبْعَثُونَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ» (they will be resurrected on the day mankind stands). It is also said that the implied form is «أَعْنِي» (I mean). It is also said that it is indeclinable (mabnī), and properly it should be genitive or nominative. The nūn in «سِجِّين» is a root letter, from «السِّجْن», which is imprisonment.
It is also said that it is a substitute for a lām.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كِتَابٌ مَرْقُومٌ (٩)).
The words of the Exalted (كِتَابٌ): i.e. it is the place of a book, because «السِّجِّين» is a place.
It is also said that the implied form is «هُوَ كِتَابٌ» (it is a book), without [any further] omission, the implied form [of the preceding] being: «وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا كِتَابُ سِجِّينٍ» (and what will make you know what the book of Sijjīn is).

ukberi-tibyan:17-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ (١٧) كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ (١٨) وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ (١٩)).
The words of the Exalted (ثُمَّ يُقَالُ): what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, explained by the clause after it. It is also said that it is the clause itself. As for «عِلِّيُّونَ», its singular is «عِلِّيّ», which is «الْمُلْك» (dominion). [Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; some sources read «الْمَلَك» (the angel).]
It is also said that it is a plural form like «عِشْرِين» (twenty) with no singular, and the implied form is: «عِلِّيُّونَ مَحَلُّ كِتَابٍ» (ʿIlliyyūn is the place of a book). It is also said that the implied form is: «مَا كِتَابُ عِلِّيِّينَ» (what is the book of ʿIlliyyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنْظُرُونَ (٢٣)).
(يَنْظُرُونَ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «الْأَبْرَار»; it may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
«عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it. It may also be a ḥāl, either from the pronoun in the genitive phrase before it, or from the agent in «يَنْظُرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ (٢٨)).
The words of the Exalted (عَيْنًا): i.e. «أَعْنِي عَيْنًا» (I mean a spring). It is also said that the implied form is «يُسْقَوْنَ عَيْنًا» (they are given to drink a spring), i.e. the water of a spring.
It is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (تَسْنِيمٍ), «تَسْنِيمٍ» being a proper name. It is also said that «تَسْنِيمٍ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it is what makes «عَيْنًا» accusative. (يَشْرَبُ بِهَا) has been discussed in [Sūrat] al-Insān.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ (٣٦)).
The words of the Exalted (هَلْ ثُوِّبَ): the clause is in an accusative position by «يَنْظُرُونَ».
It is also said that it has no position. It is also said that the implied form is: «يُقَالُ لَهُمْ: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ» (it will be said to them: have [the disbelievers] been repaid). And Allah knows best.
